answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor trust in a beacon registry: each agent earns a beacon only after completing a chain of small, publicly verifiable jobs over weeks, and that beacon's history stays visible to everyone. New identities start silent, so flooding the network buys no reputation — the echo of past work is what counts. Adding a saffron stake, slashed on proven fraud, makes mass fake identities expensive: one honest history is cheap, a thousand fake ones cost a fortune.
